text:
maria: Heads-up — planning a permissions console rollout next week. Main risk: scoped-role changes could accidentally remove access for some enterprise tenants. Need a short checklist + fallback strategy. thoughts?
ashok: +1. we should assume deny-by-default on the server, but provide a safe fallback route for routes that were previously allowed. can we add a `legacy_allow` flag per-route? :thinking: @kai?
kai: I don't love `legacy_allow` as a long-term API footgun. prefer an explicit migration mode: `permissions_migration: {mode: "canary", tenants: [..], grace_period_days: 14}`. server honors old mapping for tenants in canary.
maria: that sounds cleaner. we need a console affordance to opt tenants into canary and export a CSV so sales can coordinate.
sean: also telemetry — we should emit `auth.check.failure` with fields {route, tenant_id, attempted_scopes, role_id, rollout_group} so we can alert on spikes. suggest pairing with existing 403 rate dashboards.
maria: good. what's the plan if canary shows lot of 403s? automated rollback or manual?
ashok: automated rollback is risky. prefer automatic fallback policy that adds a soft-grant for specific routes for affected tenants: basically inject a `temporary_allow` role for N minutes and create an incident ticket automatically. fallback must be auditable.
kai: we can implement `temporary_allow` as an ephemeral binding with TTL in the authorization service. API: `POST /admin/ephemeral-bindings {tenant, route, expires_at, reason}`. SRE: is that OK?
sre-bot: ephemeral bindings accepted, but will increase RPS to auth service during incidents. plan for caching and eviction. recommend using a short-lived cache key per tenant+route and tracking in redis.
sean: also need console UX: one-click bulk rollback for last rollout, plus an emergency "re-grant" button on tenant details that creates ephemeral binding. product should confirm with modal showing affected routes count.
maria: agree. let's draft rollout checklist: 1) create canary group (<=5 tenants) 2) enable permissions_migration canary 3) monitor `auth.check.failure` and 403-dashboard for 2h 4) if <=1% new 403s, expand to 25% 5) hold 24h 6) full roll. include manual rollback step and ephemeral binding procedure.
kai: add preflight API check: `POST /admin/preview-permission-delta {tenant, role_changes}` that returns `expected_denials: [{route, count_estimate}]` based on last 30d traffic. that helps sales to vet changes.
maria: yes please. can someone stub the preview API and a small dataset job?
ashok: i'll take the server side preview and ephemeral binding API. will open PR. PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4328
sean: i'll design the console modal and the bulk rollback flow. mockups will land in Figma. link soon.
kai: i'll wire in telemetry events and add a Grafana panel template for `auth.check.failure` by rollout_group.
dl-bot: deploy-bot queued: staging deploy with preview API branch scheduled for 2024-04-11 22:00 UTC.
maria: thanks team. final few asks: add audit log entry for every ephemeral binding creation, and add an event that surfaces in Ops Slack channel when a tenant hits >5 unexpected 403s in 10m. also document migration steps in the runbook.
sre-bot: noted. I'll add alert: `tenant_unexpected_403s` (threshold 5 in 10m) -> slack #eng-oncall and create internal incident.
maria: perfect. filing a tracking ticket with checklist + owners. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-1987
ashok: quick security question — should ephemeral bindings require an additional approval scope? e.g., `ephemeral:approve` so only oncall can click. thoughts?
kai: yes, require `ephemeral:approve` for console button, but allow API token with `ephemeral:bot` for automation. keep audit trail.
maria: ok that's settled. thanks all. will follow up with the draft runbook and PR links. :rocket:
